listenings.text: I got my first job by accident, and I still tell the story wrong on purpose, because the true version is embarrassing. I was nineteen. I did not study anything useful, I did not know anybody in the company, and I did not want that job at all. I went to the interview because my mother asked me to go, and because it was raining and I had nothing else to do that afternoon. The woman who interviewed me asked one question. She asked what I did when something went wrong. I told her about a night the year before, when the shop where I worked flooded and I stayed until four in the morning moving boxes. She did not ask anything else. She said, you start on Monday. I stayed eleven years. I learned everything I know there, and I still send her a message every December.

We moved when I was nine, and nobody asked me. My father got a job three hundred kilometres away and that was it. I remember the day very clearly. It rained, the truck was late, and my mother cried in the kitchen when she thought nobody could see her. I did not cry. I was nine and I thought the whole thing was an adventure. It stopped being an adventure in about a week. I did not know anybody at the new school, I did not understand the way they spoke, and for two months I ate lunch on my own. Then a boy called Tiago sat down next to me and asked if I wanted half his sandwich, and that was the end of the problem. We are still friends. Thirty years later, if you ask me where I am from, I say the new city. But if you ask me where my childhood is, that is somewhere else entirely.

Here is something strange about memory. You do not remember the good days. You remember the days that were different. Ask anybody about last February and they will tell you nothing at all, because last February was Tuesday after Tuesday after Tuesday. But ask them about the week they moved house, or the day the dog arrived, or the first time they travelled somewhere alone, and they will give you the weather, the smell, and the shoes they wore. Those days survived because nothing about them was automatic. So if you look back at a whole year and it feels empty, the year was not empty. It was just very regular. And that is fixable. You do not need a bigger life. You need about four days in it that were not like the others.
